# Install wedge on Kali Linux (rolling)

> Tested on 2026-10-31 with wedge 0.1.1 in a clean `kalilinux/kali-rolling` container (kalilinux/kali-rolling@sha256:ea20024e16833dab1a5337f5998602f3b81f8a38f3b0995dda272c83a1b0c1b9) by `scripts/test-install.ps1`. The service-manager step is not run there (containers have no init system); wedge runs as the `wedge` user instead.

## 1. Prerequisites

```sh
command -v curl >/dev/null || (sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y curl)
```

## 2. Download and verify

Download the package and the checksum list from the GitHub release, and check the
package before installing it. Never pipe a download straight into a shell.

```sh
VERSION=0.1.1
BASE=https://github.com/alinganpatra20004/wedge/releases/download/v$VERSION
curl -fLO "$BASE/wedge_${VERSION}-1_amd64.deb"
curl -fLO "$BASE/SHA256SUMS"
grep " wedge_${VERSION}-1_amd64.deb$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c -
```

The command must print `OK`. You can also check the build provenance:

```sh
gh attestation verify wedge_${VERSION}-1_amd64.deb --repo alinganpatra20004/wedge
```

## 3. Install

```sh
sudo apt-get install -y ./wedge_${VERSION}-1_amd64.deb
```

The package creates the `wedge` system user (no login shell), installs the
binary to `/usr/bin/wedge`, the configuration to `/etc/wedge/` (root:wedge,
mode 0750/0640) and the systemd unit. Upgrades keep your configuration.

## 4. Configure

The default configuration serves a test page on `127.0.0.1:8080` only. Edit
`/etc/wedge/wedge.toml` (see the [configuration reference](../guide/configuration.md)),
then check it:

```sh
sudo wedge check-config -c /etc/wedge/wedge.toml
```

## 5. Start

```sh
sudo systemctl enable --now wedge
```

## 6. Check

```sh
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

Expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and an `x-content-type-options: nosniff` header.

## Reload after configuration changes

```sh
sudo systemctl reload wedge
```

## Remove

```sh
sudo apt-get remove wedge
```
